how_customers_find_and_choose: Homeowners search the map listing, read reviews and look at photos of finished jobs before calling
Property seekers start with online listings, photos and short video walkthroughs, then move to chat or a call with the agent
Referrals from neighbours, friends and previous clients remain the strongest source for trades and contractors
Business and building clients choose on past projects, response speed and clear written scope
Customers expect a visit or a clear written estimate soon after the first contact
what_works_now: A short gallery of finished jobs with before and after photos, shared in chat on request
A written scope, timeline and payment milestones agreed before work starts
Sharing progress photos with the client during a project without being asked
A reply within hours to every enquiry, with a clear next step such as a site visit
A saved list of past clients asked for a review once the job is complete
For agents and developers: honest, current listings with clear photos and a short video tour
A simple log of service dates for contract customers, with a reminder when the next visit is due
outdated_or_weak: Cold-calling and pamphlets in neighbourhoods as the main source of work
Verbal estimates and promises with nothing in writing
Listings with old photos or properties already sold
Generic advice to 'build a brand' with no projects shown
Claiming a finished look with only renderings and no real photos

PK: Cash on delivery and cash at the counter are still common; bank transfer and mobile wallet payments are now normal for many customers
Ramadan and the two Eids reshape demand, opening hours and staff availability every year
Summer heat, monsoon rain and power cuts affect operations and footfall
Customers often write in Urdu, Roman Urdu or a regional language, and chat is the usual first contact
Raw material price changes, summer heat and monsoon rain affect schedules
Informal contracts and advance payments are common; written scope protects both sides
Approvals from the local development authority are a touchpoint the owner confirms with the authority
UAE: Customers are multilingual and expect quick replies in chat; card and tap payments are normal
Winter is the busy season; many residents travel in summer so demand can dip
Ramadan and Eid change hours and buying patterns; the licence a business holds decides what it may sell and advertise, so the owner checks that with the licensing body
Property and fit-out activity follow the market cycle; developers and agents are regulated by the real estate authority
Tenancy and facility rules are set by the authority or the building owner; the owner confirms specifics
CA: Customers expect online booking or enquiry, card and bank e-transfer payment, and clear written confirmation
Long winters and a short summer peak shape outdoor and seasonal trades
English and French (in Quebec) matter, and many communities prefer their own language; consent for marketing messages and sales tax rules vary, so the owner checks them with a professional
Building codes, permits and licences apply to trades and are checked with the local authority or licensing body
Winter shuts down outdoor work; spring and summer are the busy months

never_assume: A website with a project gallery
Past project photos kept in one place
Staff who answer enquiries full time
